tasks.title: Train Platform Signal Check
tasks.prompt:
A small train station has two platforms. A 6x6 grid represents the station layout. The grid is given as six lines of six characters each. Characters are '.' for empty track, 'T' for a train currently on a track cell, 'S' for a signal post, and 'X' for a blocked track. The grid is:

....S.
..T...
......
.S...T
...X..
T.....

Write a program that performs the following checks and prints results in the exact format shown below.

1. Count how many trains ('T') are on the grid. Call this trainCount.
2. Count how many cells are blocked ('X'). Call this blockedCount.
3. For each train, find the Manhattan distance to the nearest signal post ('S'). Compute the average of these nearest-signal distances across all trains, rounded to 2 decimal places. Call this avgDist.

Blocked: <blockedCount>
AvgSignalDist: <avgDist to 2 decimal places>
TrainsInBlockedRow: <rowBlockedCount>

Blocked: 1

TrainsInBlockedRow: 0

tasks.title: Library Book Cart Queue
tasks.prompt:
A librarian pushes a cart holding up to 3 books at a time. The cart is a queue: books are added at the back and removed from the front. The cart starts empty.

6. remove

8. remove
9. remove

tasks.title: Laundry Room Machine Timers
tasks.prompt:
A shared laundry room has 3 washing machines (M1, M2, M3). Each machine runs one load at a time. Loads arrive at fixed times (minutes) and each has a wash duration (minutes). Machines are assigned in strict round-robin order (M1, M2, M3, M1, M2, ...) to arriving loads regardless of whether the machine is free; if the assigned machine is busy, the load waits until that machine frees up.

Loads in arrival order:
1. Towels, arrive 0, 30 min
2. Shirts, arrive 5, 25 min
3. Jeans, arrive 8, 40 min
4. Socks, arrive 15, 20 min
5. Sheets, arrive 20, 35 min
6. Uniforms, arrive 25, 25 min

Start time is 0. For each load, startTime = max(arrivalTime, assignedMachineFreeTime), endTime = startTime + duration. Update that machine's free time to endTime.

Print one line per load: "<name> <machine> <startMin> <endMin>".

After all loads, print one line per machine in order M1, M2, M3: "<machine> <idleMin>" where idleMin is the total minutes that machine sat free between time 0 and the moment the last load in the whole system finished (the global end time). A machine's idle time = globalEndTime - (sum of its load durations) - (time before its first load started, if any). More precisely: idleMin = globalEndTime - (its first load's start time) - (sum of its load durations).

Print 6 + 3 = 9 lines total, no extra spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Towels M1 0 30
Shirts M2 5 30
Jeans M3 8 48
Socks M1 30 50
Sheets M2 30 65
Uniforms M3 48 73
M1 23
M2 8
M3 0
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Robot Warehouse Orientation Matrix

[0, 1]

[-1, 0]

Write a program that:

2. Multiplies the final matrix by the vector [3, 5] (treating [3,5] as a column vector) to get a new position offset.

4. Determines if the final matrix equals the original R0 (YES or NO).

Final: <four values as a,b,c,d representing the 2x2 matrix rows, no spaces, e.g. 0,1,-1,0>
Offset: <x,y as integers with a comma, no spaces>
Manhattan: <integer>
SameAsStart: <YES or NO>

tasks.title: Train Route Transfer Cost Matrix
tasks.prompt:
A regional train operator has 5 stops numbered 0-4. A fare matrix F[i][j] gives the cost in dollars for a ticket from stop i to stop j (F[i][i] = 0, and some pairs have no direct service, shown as 0):
F =
[0, 3, 0, 5, 0]
[3, 0, 4, 0, 7]
[0, 4, 0, 6, 0]
[5, 0, 6, 0, 8]
[0, 7, 0, 8, 0]

A traveler wants to go from stop 0 to stop 4. They can take a direct ticket if available, or a one-transfer ticket via one intermediate stop k (k not 0 or 4): cost = F[0][k] + F[k][4].

Write a program that:
1. Finds the cheapest total fare from stop 0 to stop 4 considering direct and all one-transfer options.
2. Counts how many of the 20 off-diagonal entries in F represent available direct service (nonzero).
3. Finds the stop (0-4, excluding 0 and 4) that would serve as the cheapest single-transfer intermediate stop (smallest index if tied). If no one-transfer route exists, output NONE.
4. Computes the most expensive direct fare among all available off-diagonal direct services.

Output exactly these 4 lines:
Cheapest: <fare in dollars, integer>
DirectCount: <count of nonzero off-diagonal entries, integer>
BestTransfer: <stop index 0-4 or NONE>
MaxDirect: <most expensive direct fare, integer>

Cheapest: 10
DirectCount: 12
BestTransfer: 1
MaxDirect: 8

A vending machine identifies products with a three-digit code. For restocking, the operator wants to know, for each code, whether it is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards) and the product of its three digits.

Product codes to process, in order: 121, 345, 565, 789, 111, 232.

Output exactly 6 lines, one per code, in the order given. Each line has the format:
CODE <code> PALINDROME <true|false> PRODUCT <product>

There is a single space between each label and its value, and no trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
CODE 121 PALINDROME true PRODUCT 2
CODE 345 PALINDROME false PRODUCT 60
CODE 565 PALINDROME true PRODUCT 150
CODE 789 PALINDROME false PRODUCT 504
CODE 111 PALINDROME true PRODUCT 1
CODE 232 PALINDROME true PRODUCT 12
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

tasks.title: Museum Exhibit Room Modular Pattern
tasks.prompt:

Rooms to process: 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.

ROOM <n> MOD5 <r> PRIME <true|false>

There is a single space between each label and its value, and no trailing spaces on any line. (Room 1 is not prime.)

ROOM 1 MOD5 1 PRIME false
ROOM 2 MOD5 2 PRIME true
ROOM 3 MOD5 3 PRIME true
ROOM 5 MOD5 0 PRIME true
ROOM 7 MOD5 2 PRIME true
ROOM 11 MOD5 1 PRIME true

tasks.title: Laundry Room Dryer Rotation
tasks.prompt:
A shared laundry room uses a circular ring buffer of capacity 4 to track the most recent dryer reservations. Each operation is a pair: the action ('RES' for reserving a slot, 'REL' for releasing the oldest reservation) and a resident number.

Operations list:
RES 10
RES 20
RES 30
REL
RES 40
RES 50
REL
RES 60
REL
RES 70
REL

A 'REL' removes the oldest reservation from the ring. If the ring is empty, 'REL' is ignored. 'RES' always adds to the ring, overwriting the oldest entry if the ring is full.

Produce the following output:

Line 1: label 'Ring contents (oldest to newest): ' followed by the resident numbers currently in the ring, separated by single spaces.
Line 2: label 'Reservations made: ' followed by the total number of 'RES' operations.
Line 3: label 'Overwritten entries: ' followed by the number of times an existing ring entry was overwritten by a new 'RES'.

Ring contents (oldest to newest): 50 60 70
Reservations made: 7
Overwritten entries: 0

tasks.title: Lighthouse Lens Rotation Counter
tasks.prompt:
A lighthouse rotates its lens through 3 positions: North (N), East (E), and South (S). The rotation follows a deterministic rule based on input signals.

The lens starts at position 'N'.

The rule for each signal:
- If the current position is 'N' and the signal is 'R', move to 'E'.
- If the current position is 'N' and the signal is 'L', move to 'S'.
- If the current position is 'E' and the signal is 'R', move to 'S'.
- If the current position is 'E' and the signal is 'L', move to 'N'.
- If the current position is 'S' and the signal is 'R', move to 'N'.
- If the current position is 'S' and the signal is 'L', move to 'E'.

The signal sequence is: "R", "R", "L", "R", "L", "L", "R"

Process each signal in order, updating the position. Count how many times the lens passes through position 'E' (i.e., the position AFTER a signal update equals 'E'). Also record the final position after all signals.

Print your output in exactly this format:
East passes: <count>
Final position: <position>

Where <count> is an integer and <position> is a single character. There is a single space after each colon.
tasks.expected_stdout:
East passes: 4
Final position: E
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Elevator Floor Request Sequencer
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program for a small office elevator that services floors 1 through 6. The elevator starts on floor 1, doors closed, and idle. It receives a fixed sequence of 16 events:
["CALL:3", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:5", "CALL:5", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:2", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:6", "CALL:6", "CALL:6", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:4"]

The events work as follows:
- "CALL:n" adds floor n to the request queue if it is not already in the queue (duplicates are ignored). If the elevator is idle and the queue is non-empty, the elevator immediately begins moving toward the first floor in the queue, one floor per tick, until it reaches it; upon arrival the elevator becomes "waiting" (doors still closed) until an OPEN event.
- "OPEN" opens the doors if the elevator is waiting at a requested floor; this removes that floor from the queue and the elevator becomes "idle". If the elevator is not waiting, OPEN does nothing.
- "CLOSE" closes the doors if they are open; otherwise does nothing.

When the elevator finishes moving to a floor and becomes "waiting", it does NOT automatically process further CALL events until an OPEN/CLOSE cycle occurs.

Output exactly 5 lines (no trailing spaces):
FinalFloor: <integer>
Doors: <Open or Closed>
QueueLength: <integer>
TotalFloorsTraveled: <integer>
VisitedFloors: <comma-separated floors in order visited, e.g. 3,5,2>

VisitedFloors lists each floor the elevator arrived at (became waiting at) in chronological order, including repeats.
tasks.expected_stdout:
FinalFloor: 4
Doors: Closed
QueueLength: 1
TotalFloorsTraveled: 13
VisitedFloors: 3,5,2,6,4
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Coffee Shop Order State Tracker
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program that tracks the state of orders at a small coffee shop counter. Each order goes through states in this fixed cycle: "Received" -> "Making" -> "Ready" -> "PickedUp" (then the order is done and removed). Only one order can be in the "Making" state at a time; if a second order tries to enter "Making" while another is making, it stays in "Received".

The shop receives a fixed sequence of 18 events:
["NEW:A", "NEW:B", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "NEW:C", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "NEW:D", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "NEW:E", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE"]

- "NEW:x" creates a new order with id x in state "Received" and appends it to the back of the queue.
- "ADVANCE" moves the front-most order that can advance one step: if the front order is "Received" and nothing is "Making", it becomes "Making"; if the front order is "Making", it becomes "Ready"; if the front order is "Ready", it becomes "PickedUp" and is removed. If no order can advance, ADVANCE does nothing.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):
Queue: <comma-separated order ids in queue order, or EMPTY>
FrontState: <state of the front order, or NONE>
Making: <order id currently Making, or NONE>
PickedUpCount: <integer>

PickedUpCount is how many orders reached "PickedUp" during the whole sequence.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Queue: E
FrontState: Making
Making: E
PickedUpCount: 4
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Vending Machine Stock Reorder Check

    {"slot": "C2", "product": "Gum", "count": 11, "price": 0.75}

Reorder count: 2
